name: Prometheus SNMP Exporter
what_it_is: A Prometheus exporter that bridges SNMP devices and Prometheus by walking OID trees defined in snmp.yml and exposing the results as Prometheus metrics. It acts as a proxy: Prometheus scrapes the exporter's /snmp endpoint with a target parameter pointing to the actual SNMP device.
components: snmp.yml (module and auth configuration, generated from MIBs)
generator (optional CLI tool to produce snmp.yml from MIBs via generator.yml)
protocols: SNMPv3 (GETBULK, with noAuthNoPriv / authNoPriv / authPriv security levels)
measurement: OID tree walks mapped to Prometheus gauge/counter metrics with SNMP table indexes as labels
ifHCOutOctets, ifDescr, ifIndex, ifName, ifAlias — standard IF-MIB interface metrics
Counter64 values auto-wrapped at 2^53 to avoid float64 rounding loss
Exporter self-metrics available at /metrics (scrape latency, errors, etc.)
Multi-module scrape: multiple modules collected in one HTTP request with configurable concurrency (--snmp.module-concurrency)
configuration: snmp.yml: top-level auths (SNMP credentials) and modules (OID walk lists, retries, timeouts, lookups)
--config.file flag supports multiple files and glob patterns (e.g. snmp*.yml)
generator.yml: simplified walk instructions fed to the generator to produce snmp.yml from MIBs
--web.config.file: TLS and HTTP basic authentication for all exporter HTTP endpoints
URL parameters: target, auth, module, snmp_context, snmp_engineid override per-scrape
max_repetitions, retries, timeout, allow_nonincreasing_oids, use_unconnected_udp_socket per module
Prometheus relabeling used to route __address__ → __param_target → exporter address
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection mechanism; the exporter surfaces SNMP walk failures as scrape errors
allow_nonincreasing_oids: true can mask out-of-order OID responses from buggy agents
max_repetitions reduction works around devices that fail on large GETBULK requests
use_unconnected_udp_socket bypasses multi-homed devices that send responses from the wrong source address
modes: Single-target mode: one exporter instance scraping a specific device per request
Multi-target proxy mode: one exporter instance serving thousands of devices via parameterised URL
Multi-module mode: comma-separated or repeated module params collected in a single scrape
Generator mode: offline MIB-to-snmp.yml compilation (separate binary, not the exporter itself)
constraints: snmp.yml MUST NOT be edited by hand for MIB-derived configs; use the generator instead
Duplicate module or auth names in snmp.yml are treated as invalid and will prevent loading
Counter64 wrap-around at 2^53 is automatic and cannot be disabled per-module; only a global --no-snmp.wrap-large-counters flag exists
Multi-module walks do NOT deduplicate overlapping OID walks between modules, potentially doubling traffic
SNMP v1/v2c community strings are transmitted in plaintext; SNMPv3 is required for confidentiality
The generator requires NetSNMP shared libraries at build time (libsnmp-dev) and cannot be run as a pure Go binary
docker_services: prom/snmp-exporter (Docker Hub) — single-container exporter, no docker-compose provided in repo
Generator Docker image supports 'make docker-generate' to produce snmp.yml without a local NetSNMP install
notable_absences: No official docker-compose.yml in the repository; users must compose their own Prometheus + snmp_exporter stack
No built-in SNMP trap receiver (snmptrapd); the exporter is poll-only
No native support for SNMP SET operations; read-only by design
No built-in label cardinality controls; unbounded table indexes can create high-cardinality metrics
